subject: KV cache eviction event — customer summary, timeline, and verification checklist
messages:

Subject: Observed increased tail latency on inference requests this morning

Hi Mina,

We started seeing a rise in tail latency and a small number of 504s against the Redwood endpoint for our LLM scoring pipeline starting around 08:45 PT. Impacted calls are primarily inference requests with long context windows (histories ~2k tokens). Can your team confirm whether there was any configuration change or rollout this morning that might explain this?

We can share logs if helpful — attaching a short sample. This is affecting some late-night settlement flows, so we’re hoping for a quick triage.

Thanks,
Amanda

Amanda — thanks for the heads up and for the sample. We’re investigating now.

Preliminary notes: we rolled a config patch to the autoscaler/eviction service at 07:30 PT that included a change to KV cache lifetime defaults intended to reduce stale entries. We did not expect visible impact, but we are seeing elevated cache miss rates in the 08:30–09:10 window for long-context requests.

We’ll correlate eviction logs and pod lifecycle events and come back with a timeline and immediate mitigations. I’ll keep you posted in 30–45 minutes.

— Mina

Subject: Re: Observed increased tail latency on inference requests this morning

Follow-up with a short technical summary and our immediate actions: 

What happened (brief):
- At 07:30 PT we deployed autoscaler change AS-7. The change unintentionally set the KV cache entry TTL used by the dtype frontends from 30 minutes to 30 seconds for certain codepaths (a default override in the rollout manifest). This dramatically increased KV cache eviction for long-history sessions.

Impact window:
- 08:26–09:05 PT: elevated cache miss ratio on Goodleaf’s request profile, leading to more KV refills and longer decode times. Tail latency spikes (95–99th percentile) and a small fraction of requests timed out (504s) under burst load.

Immediate mitigations we executed:
- 09:10 PT: rolled back AS-7 and restored the KV TTL to 30 minutes for the affected frontends (rollback completed by 09:18 PT).
- 09:20 PT: temporarily increased autoscaler headroom on the Goodleaf-serving pool to soften burst effects.
- 09:25 PT: enabled additional request-level retries with a capped backoff for long-context requests.

Customer-facing impact:
- Observed increased 95/99 latency for ~39 minutes, and ~0.6% of Goodleaf’s calls returned 504s during the peak window.

Next steps (we’ll own these and share timelines):
1) Detailed RCA doc and technical appendix (in progress) — ETA 2027-11-22 17:00 PT — Dylan (owner).
2) Post-deployment guard: add a CI check to prevent TTL regressions in rollout manifests — ETA 2027-12-05 — Irene (owner).
3) Customer verification checklist and runbook artifacts for Goodleaf to confirm recovered flows — ETA 2027-11-23 — Mina (owner).
4) Goodwill remediation: offering a pro-rated usage credit for the impacted window; will propose amount after internal approval — Mina (owner).

Amanda — apologies for the disruption. We’ll attach the timeline CSV and RC appendix in the detailed note. Please let us know if you want a short sync.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@goodleaf.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-21T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: KV cache eviction event — RCA summary, timeline, and verification checklist

Amanda — thank you again for your patience this morning. Attached is a concise customer-facing postmortem and verification checklist. Below is the executive summary and concrete action items we would like Goodleaf to complete to confirm full recovery.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: a rollout manifest override in autoscaler change AS-7 set a KV cache TTL to 30s for specific frontend codepaths handling long-context sessions. The shorter TTL caused frequent cache evictions, increasing KV refills and GPU decode work for long-history requests, which in turn raised tail latency and produced a small number of timeouts under burst load.
- Impact: 08:26–09:05 PT on 2027-11-21 — increased 95/99 latency for affected request patterns; ~0.6% 504 rate on Goodleaf production traffic. No data exfiltration or integrity issues were detected.
- Resolution: AS-7 rollback completed by 09:18 PT; autoscaler headroom increased and retries enabled. Latency metrics returned to baseline within ~20 minutes of the rollback.

Attachments delivered with this email:
- rca_technical_appendix.pdf — full technical details, traces, and root-cause proofing.
- kvcache_eviction_timeline.csv — minute-level timeline of eviction rates, pod events, and customer request errors.
- customer_verification_checklist.xlsx — checklist for Goodleaf to run verification steps and confirm recovery.

Requested verification steps for Goodleaf (short):
1) Run the included verification script (sheet 1 in checklist) against your late-night settlement batch in a staging slice and confirm 95/99 latency is within expected baselines. (Owner: Goodleaf Ops)
2) Confirm no application-level retries masked errors in your logs during the window (Owner: Goodleaf Engineering).
3) Share a small sample of pre/post metrics for 07:30–10:00 PT to validate our timeline (Owner: Amanda).

Action items and owners (Redwood):
- Dylan: deliver full RCA doc and kernel traces (ETA 2027-11-22 17:00 PT).
- Irene: create guardrail CI test for TTL/eviction defaults; add a manifest lint (ETA 2027-12-05).
- Mina: propose goodwill credit and send a formal credit note after finance review (ETA 2027-11-24).

Compensation and SLA note: we recognize the operational impact and will propose a pro-rated credit for the impacted token and request volume. We will also place additional rollout gates for TTL-related changes for all customers with long-context usage patterns.

If you’d like a short 30-minute review call (engineering + ops), we can schedule one tomorrow. Please tell us a preferred window.

Thanks — and again, sincerely sorry for the interruption. We value Goodleaf as a customer and will follow through on the items above.

— Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
